blocks.intro: A clog clears and stays clear. These point to damage in the pipe itself:

tiles.h3: The Camera Shows a Belly or Break

blocks.h2: Why Sewer Lines Fail in Mokena
blocks.intro: More than half of Mokena's homes went up between 1990 and 2009, so most sewer lines in town are PVC, not clay. They fail differently.

items.body: A trench backfilled during construction can keep settling for years. The pipe sags with it, and water and paper sit in the low spot until the line clogs.
Shifting soil can separate PVC joints just enough for roots and sand to get in.

items.h3: Trees That Grew Up With the Subdivision
items.body: The parkway and yard trees planted in the 1990s are now big enough to send roots toward any loose joint.
About 1 in 8 Mokena homes was built before 1970. Those lines can be clay or cast iron, with the root and crack problems that come with age.

blocks.h2: How We Repair a Sewer Line
blocks.intro: Once we know what's wrong, there's usually more than one way to fix it. Which method makes sense depends on the pipe's condition, location, and how it failed.
head: Method
What It Involves
Typical Disruption
rows: A resin-coated liner is pulled through the existing pipe and cured in place, creating a new pipe inside the old one.
Minimal digging, usually just small access points
A new pipe is pulled through the old one while a bursting head fractures the old pipe outward to make room.
Minimal digging, works even when the old pipe is badly damaged
The damaged section is dug up and replaced directly.
More digging, but sometimes the only option depending on damage location and access
blocks.note: In Mokena subdivisions, the sewer often runs under a driveway, a paver patio or a finished landscape bed. The camera tells us which method avoids tearing them out.

blocks.h2: Sewer Repair Questions From Mokena Homeowners

items.q: My house is only 25 years old. Why does the sewer line need repair?
items.answer: Usually because the soil under the pipe settled after construction and left a sag, or a joint pulled apart. Newer pipe doesn't crack like old clay, but it can still sag and collect debris. A [camera inspection](/mokena/video-camera-sewer-inspections) shows exactly where.

items.q: Can you fix a sag without replacing the whole line?
items.answer: Often. If the rest of the line is in good shape, we dig at the low spot, reset the pipe at the right slope and leave the rest alone.

items.q: Is sewer line replacement ever the better choice?
items.preview: When damage runs the length of the line.
items.answer: When the camera shows several breaks, a collapsed section or an old clay line in poor shape from end to end, replacing it once costs less than fixing it piece by piece.

items.q: Who is responsible for the sewer line in Mokena?
items.preview: Usually the homeowner, from the house to the main.
items.answer: In most cases the homeowner owns the line from the house to the public sewer. If the camera shows the problem is in the village main, we'll tell you so you can report it.

items.q: How much does sewer line repair cost in Mokena?
items.preview: It depends on the damage and the method. You'll approve a flat price first.
items.answer: It depends on what the camera finds, how deep the line is, the repair method and what sits on top of it. You'll see and approve a flat-rate price before any work begins.
